answers.answer: Reveal the top region card to place the King; each player takes another region card for their home region and places their Grande there. Initial ten: two in home beside the Grande, one on the first success-track space, seven in court.
answers.evidence: Setup: reveal the top card and put the King in that region; another region card determines home; ten are two home, one on track, seven in court.

answers.answer: In round 1 the chosen starter begins. In later rounds, the player who took the last turn in the preceding round begins. Others play clockwise. No power-card value already played that round may be matched.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 2: chosen starter; later, player who took the last turn; others clockwise; no value already played may be matched.

answers.answer: Players take turns in descending power-card value. At the start of your turn, recruit up to the Caballero allowance pictured on your power card from provinces into court. Recruitment happens before choosing an action card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 3–4: turns in descending value; at start of turn recruit up to the pictured amount; after recruitment choose an action card.

answers.answer: If your provinces lack enough of your color, you may take your own Caballeros from the board to make up the difference. The King's region is taboo and the Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 3: take your own from the board to make up the difference; King's region remains taboo and Castillo cannot supply pieces outside general scoring.

answers.answer: Ordinary deployment moves from your court to regions adjacent to the King's current region and/or the Castillo; you may divide the allowance freely. The printed number is a maximum, so you may deploy fewer or none. It may be split among destinations.
answers.evidence: Actions: number is a maximum; deploy fewer, including none; move from court to adjacent regions and/or Castillo, dividing allowance freely.

answers.answer: Yes, do the ordinary deployment and special action in either order. Complete one activity before starting the other; neither may be split or interleaved. The special action may be declined.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 4: either order, complete one activity before the other; neither split or interleaved; may decline special action.

answers.answer: After a player's turn, lay aside the selected card so later players cannot choose it. After all players take a turn, discard remaining face-up cards. The King card is revealed again every round and is never permanently discarded.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 5: selected card laid aside; remaining face-up cards discarded after all turns; King card revealed again and never permanently discarded.

answers.answer: No Caballero, Grande, or mobile scoreboard may move into or out of the King's region. It may still be scored. An action that moves the King changes which region is protected.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: King's region is taboo to Caballeros, Grandes, mobile scoreboards; it may still be scored; moving the King changes protected region.

answers.answer: Announce clearly how many Caballeros are put inside. Any or all may enter regardless of the King's location. No action removes them; they leave only during general scoring.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: adding/moving Caballeros, any or all may go into Castillo regardless of King; announce number; leave only during general scoring.

answers.answer: General scoring occurs after rounds 3, 6, and 9. In order: players secretly choose one legal region destination for all their Castillo Caballeros, with disks face down, before the Castillo is uncovered; score the Castillo; reveal disks and move pieces out to chosen regions (or court for an illegal King's-region choice); replace the empty Castillo; then score the nine regions in scoring-track order and record points.
answers.evidence: General scoring stages 1–4 give timing and order; destination selection precedes lifting the Castillo.

answers.answer: A player's Castillo pieces must all go to one region, not split. The King's region is prohibited. Pieces cannot be kept in the Castillo; it is emptied. If it was illegally selected, those pieces go to that player's court.
answers.evidence: General scoring: all Castillo Caballeros go to one region; King's region prohibited; move every player's pieces; illegal King choice sends pieces to court; none retained or split.

answers.answer: The three tied leaders each score 3 points (second-place value), and the player with three Caballeros scores 1 (third-place value). Grandes do not count toward majority; they contribute zero Caballeros.
answers.evidence: Example on 5/3/1: 4,4,4,3 score 3,3,3,1; only Caballeros count, Grande contributes zero.

answers.answer: The players with counts 4 and 3 score 6 and 4; the two players tied at 2 score zero each.
answers.evidence: Publisher example on 6/4/2: counts 4,3,2,2 score 6,4,0,0.

answers.answer: In a two-player game only first place can pay; in a three-player game first and second can pay. A two-player tie for first shifts to second place, which is beyond the two-player payable ranks, so neither scores.
answers.evidence: Region ranks: two players only first; three players first and second; two-player tie for first pays neither after cutoff.

answers.answer: Whenever the relevant region is scored, including special scoring, the sole majority holder gets +2 for being in the King's region and the sole majority holder with their own Grande there gets +2 home bonus. Neither bonus applies on a tie for first.
answers.evidence: Bonuses apply whenever region is scored including special scorings; King's +2, Home +2; neither awarded on tie for first.

answers.answer: Specially scoring the Castillo does not empty or redistribute it. Uncover and score it, then cover the same Caballeros again; redistribution waits until general scoring.
answers.evidence: Protected locations and Stack 3: score contents then cover them again without redistribution; same pieces remain.

answers.answer: A mobile scoreboard may be placed at the Castillo. It cannot move into or out of the King's region, cannot be stacked on the other scoreboard, and cannot be reversed or rotated to change values.
answers.evidence: Stack 4: Castillo allowed; no movement into/out of King's region; scoreboards cannot stack; place right side up, never reversed or rotated.

answers.answer: Move your Grande to another region except the King's region or Castillo; it cannot leave the King's region. The destination may already have several Grandes. It becomes your new home region.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Grande: destination exclusions, cannot leave King's region, destination may contain several Grandes, destination becomes new home.

answers.answer: Return any one of your played power cards to your hand, including the card played this turn. You need not reveal which, although taking the visible top card is apparent.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Power Cards: any one played card including this turn; need not reveal which; visible top card apparent.

answers.answer: The game ends after completing all stages of the third general scoring, after round 9. The player furthest along the success track wins. No additional tiebreaker is given.
answers.evidence: End: finish third general scoring after round 9; furthest along track wins; no additional tiebreaker.

answers.answer: Separate action cards into stacks by the 1–5 Caballeros printed on their backs, shuffle each stack separately, and place face down. At the start of each round reveal the top card of each of five stacks (five choices). The standard round marker starts at 1.
answers.evidence: Setup: stacks by 1–5, shuffle separately, marker at 1; Turn Structure: reveal top card of each of five action stacks.

answers.answer: A played power card is not returned to hand; it stays in that player's face-up used stack, with only the top card visible. A special action can recover a played card.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure 2: played cards remain in face-up used stack with only top visible, rather than returning to hand; special action can recover one.

answers.answer: If the King is moved before ordinary deployment, the new King position determines adjacent destinations. The King card places the King in any region except the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Protected locations: use King's new position if moved before deployment; Stack 5: King may go in any region except Castillo.

answers.answer: Put the Veto card before you and retain it. It can stop one special action during this round or the next; it cannot stop that action card's ordinary deployment.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 Veto: retain before you; stop one special action this or next round; cannot stop ordinary deployment portion.

answers.answer: While Veto is held, players must announce special actions before executing them. Object as soon as the player starts: you may stop an announced action before execution or prevent the remaining part of an incomplete action. A completed action cannot be vetoed; already executed parts are not undone, and you may prevent just part.
answers.evidence: Veto instructions specify announcement, object timing, incomplete actions, completed actions, and partial prevention.

answers.answer: Discard Veto after using it once. If unused, discard it at the end of the next round.
answers.evidence: Veto: discard after using once; if unused, discard at end of next round.

answers.answer: Every fellow player sends all Caballeros in their court to the provinces; the selecting player is unaffected. A player with an empty court sends none.
answers.evidence: Decay of Authority—all court: every fellow player sends all court Caballeros to provinces; empty court sends none; selecting player unaffected.

answers.answer: The fellow player with two sends all two to the provinces; the selecting player is unaffected, so their five remain.
answers.evidence: Decay of Authority—three from court: send three or all if fewer than three; selecting player unaffected.

answers.answer: The detailed paragraph and card face require each player, including the selecting player, to send three of their own Caballeros to the provinces. Starting with the player to the selecting player's left, proceed clockwise, with the selecting player last. Pieces may come from any regions and/or that player's court, never the King's region or Castillo. The summary gives no shortfall rule if fewer than three eligible pieces exist. The bold heading instead says “fellow players.”
answers.evidence: The King returns detailed execution and heading discrepancy are both explicitly stated in Stack 2.

answers.answer: The selecting player chooses one Caballero from a region for each player, including themselves, and returns each to its owner's provinces. Pieces cannot come from courts, the King's region, or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Send one from each player: selecting player chooses one regional piece for every player including self; court, King's region and Castillo excluded.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly chooses one region on their disk; choices are simultaneous and revealed together. The region must contain at least two of that player's Caballeros; choose such a region and return two to the provinces. King's region and Castillo cannot be used.
answers.evidence: Secretly remove two: disk choices simultaneous; region must contain at least two own; return two; never take from King's region or Castillo.

answers.answer: Choose a region containing one of that player's Caballeros and return that one to the provinces.
answers.evidence: The singleton fallback applies when the player has at most one in every region: choose a region with one and return that one.

answers.answer: Each affected fellow player secretly selects a region on their disk with at least one of their Caballeros; selections are simultaneous and revealed together. They return all their own pieces there to the provinces. A player with none in any region is unaffected.
answers.evidence: Secretly remove all from one region: simultaneous disk selection; choose region with at least one; return all own there; none in any region is unaffected.

answers.answer: Yes, choose any region, including the King's region, or the Castillo. Use normal region-scoring rules, applicable rank limits, and bonuses. Scoring the Castillo does not redistribute its pieces; uncover and score, then cover the same pieces again.
answers.evidence: Stack 2 pick one region: any including King's region or Castillo, normal scoring; Castillo covered again without redistribution.

answers.answer: The printed 4-value group is Galicia (4/2/0), Catalonia (4/2/1), and Seville (4/3/1). Eligibility is determined by the current first value, with mobile scoreboards replacing printed values. Thus Galicia at 8/4/0 does not qualify; Granada at 4/0/0 does. Applicable bonuses apply to special scoring.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 all 4-value: regions whose current first value is 4; mobile replaces printed values; examples exclude Galicia with 8/4/0 and add Granada with 4/0/0; special scorings get bonuses.

answers.answer: Printed 5-value group: Basque Country, Aragon, Valencia. Printed 6- and 7-value group: Old Castile (6), New Castile (7), Granada (6). Eligibility uses each region's current first value, so mobile scoreboards can remove a printed member or add another region whose current first value fits. Castillo is not included in all-5 scoring.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 lists printed groups and says current first value determines eligibility; mobile scoreboard replaces printed values; all-5 says Castillo is not scored.

answers.answer: Only sole first places score; ties for first score nothing because they would normally receive second-place value. Other ranks receive nothing. Castillo is excluded.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 first-position-only: sole first places score; tie for first gets nothing; other ranks nothing; excludes Castillo.

answers.answer: Score all board regions tied for the most total Caballeros. Castillo is not considered or scored, even if it contains more than either region.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 most-Caballeros: score all regions tied for most; Castillo neither considered nor scored.

answers.answer: Compare nonempty board regions; score all regions tied for the least. Empty regions and the Castillo are neither considered nor scored.
answers.evidence: Stack 3 least-Caballeros: compare nonempty board regions; all tied for least score; empty regions and Castillo excluded.

answers.answer: All fellow players move all their own Caballeros out of the chosen region. Each secretly chooses another region using their disk; reveal choices simultaneously. If a player chooses the King's region or the region being vacated, that player's pieces go to their court instead. Pieces cannot be taken out of the King's region, and Castillo cannot be emptied by this card.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Movement describes whose pieces leave, secret simultaneous destinations, court fallback, and taboo/ Castillo restrictions.

answers.answer: Royal Adviser moves the King to a neighboring region, at most one region away. The King card may place him in any region except the Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 Royal Adviser: neighboring region; Stack 5 King: any region except Castillo.

answers.answer: The Court moves two of your own Caballeros from provinces to court. This is separate from the card's normal deployment of up to four from court to board; either completed activity may come first. The summary gives no shortfall procedure if provinces cannot supply two.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 The Court and Turn Structure: two own from provinces to court; separate from ordinary up-to-four deployment; either activity first; shortfall unspecified.

answers.answer: All players secretly choose regions on disks and reveal simultaneously. Score each uniquely chosen region under normal rules; if multiple players chose a region, it is not scored. Disk includes nine board regions, including the King's region, but not Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 4: secret disk choices/reveal simultaneously; score uniquely chosen regions; duplicates not scored; disk regions include King but not Castillo.

answers.answer: You may take all your own Caballeros from one region and distribute them among other regions and/or Castillo; you may return some to the original region. The origin excludes the King's region and Castillo; destinations exclude the King's region but may include Castillo. Ordinary deployment still follows adjacency restrictions.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 all-own-from-one-region explicitly permits return to original; all relocation origins exclude King/Castillo and destinations exclude King but may include Castillo.

answers.answer: Up to two additional Caballeros from court may be deployed by the special action, so together with the normal deployment of up to one, up to three enter the board. The two special-action pieces may go to any non-King regions and/or Castillo; only the normal piece requires adjacency.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 two more from court: up to two additional to any non-King regions/Castillo; normal one means up to three; only normal one requires adjacency.

answers.answer: Choose one of the two special alternatives, not both: either two more from court or all your own Caballeros from one region. Normal deployment of up to one still applies.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 choice card: choose one preceding special action, not both; normal deployment still applies.

answers.answer: Up to five own and/or foreign Caballeros may be taken from one origin region only, then distributed to other non-King regions and/or Castillo. They cannot come from multiple origin regions.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 up to five: own and/or foreign from one origin region, distributed to other non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: You may move up to three foreign Caballeros, from any non-King board regions and possibly multiple origins; you cannot include your own pieces. Destinations may be any non-King regions and/or Castillo.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 any three foreign: up to three other players' pieces, any non-King board regions, multiple origins, never Castillo as source; destinations any non-King regions/Castillo.

answers.answer: Any three: up to three own and/or foreign Caballeros, from any non-King origin regions, to any non-King regions and/or Castillo. Any four: up to four own and/or foreign, from any non-King origins to other non-King regions and/or Castillo; the summary preserves the ‘other regions’ destination restriction for this four-piece card.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 differentiates any three's any non-King destinations from any four's other non-King destinations; both allow own/foreign and non-King origins.

answers.answer: Move up to two of your own plus up to two foreign Caballeros; these are separate ownership allowances. Pieces may come from any origin regions except the King's region or Castillo. Destinations may be any non-King region and/or Castillo, under the general restrictions applying to all Intrigue entries.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 says up to two of your own plus two foreign from any regions; its general paragraph excludes the King's region and Castillo as origins, allows non-King regions and/or Castillo as destinations, and says all entries remain subject to those rules.

answers.answer: Move up to four of your own Caballeros only, from any non-King origin regions into other non-King regions and/or Castillo. The destination must be an ‘other’ region; Castillo is a permitted destination.
answers.evidence: Stack 1 any four own: up to four own only, any non-King origins into other non-King regions and/or Castillo.

answers.answer: The secret-choice scoring action allows any of the nine board regions, including the King's region, but not Castillo. The card letting its player pick one location allows any region including King's region or Castillo, and Castillo is scored without redistribution.
answers.evidence: Stack 4 each secretly chooses: disk includes nine regions and excludes Castillo; Stack 2 pick one region: includes King's region or Castillo.

answers.answer: Both mobile scoreboards begin beside the board. The special action may introduce a scoreboard from beside the board or move one already on the board to a different region.
answers.evidence: Components: place both mobile scoreboards beside the board; Stack 4 mobile scoreboard: introduce from beside board or move one on board to a different region.
